meta.title: AI Infrastructure Deal Database
meta.subtitle: Financing structures, credit support, and transactions behind the compute buildout
meta.coverage: Project and structured financings, credit support instruments, platform M&A, and the long term power contracts underpinning data centre capacity
meta.method: Built from primary sources: company press releases, SEC filings, earnings calls, and reporting from Bloomberg, CNBC, DCD, and the Financial Times. Every figure carries a provenance tag: disclosed, computed from disclosed, analyst imputed, or not disclosed. Ratios are computed, never taken from secondary summaries.
meta.sourcePolicy: Each record links to the primary source where a stable public URL exists, normally the company press release or filing. Where a record is drawn from subscription reporting or where no stable link exists, the source is named in the record and no link is shown rather than linking to an aggregator.
meta.sortNote: Deals are listed newest first within each section, by announcement date. Where only a month or year is public, the date is set to the first of that period and flagged as approximate.

ppaDeals.name: Project Kilby
ppaDeals.note: Vertically integrated gas to compute. Chevron builds, owns, operates generation behind the fence.
ppaDeals.summary: Chevron is building 2.7 gigawatts of gas fired power in West Texas that feeds a Microsoft data centre directly, bypassing the public grid and its multi year connection queue.

ppaDeals.name: Terrestrial Energy and Riot Platforms
ppaDeals.parties: Terrestrial Energy (Nasdaq: IMSR) and Riot Platforms (Nasdaq: RIOT)
ppaDeals.type: Memorandum of understanding, co located nuclear and data centres
ppaDeals.instrument: Memorandum of understanding. No purchased megawatts, no offtake, no committed capacity.
ppaDeals.structure: MOU to develop co located IMSR plants alongside Riot developed data centres. Multiple 390MW IMSR plants representing up to 4GW of nuclear capacity. Candidate sites include existing Riot facilities in Texas and Kentucky. Includes potential to incorporate natural gas as a bridge fuel for commercial operations on an accelerated timeline.
ppaDeals.status: MOU only. Terrestrial Energy is engaged with regulators and expects to build, license and commission first IMSR plants in the early 2030s.
ppaDeals.note: This is the weakest instrument in the nuclear set and it carries the second largest headline number. An MOU to consider project opportunities at candidate sites is not contracted capacity. It appears in trackers at 4GW alongside operating plant PPAs, which is the clearest illustration of why instrument classification matters more than capacity totals.

provenance.disclosed: MOU signed, up to 4GW across multiple 390MW IMSR plants, candidate sites in Texas and Kentucky, gas as potential bridge fuel, first plants targeted early 2030s
provenance.notDisclosed: any binding commitment, capital, offtake, site selection, timeline

ppaDeals.summary: A non binding agreement to explore building reactors next to data centres in Texas and Kentucky, carrying a 4 gigawatt headline figure but no commitment.

ppaDeals.name: Wichita & Mustang Creek
ppaDeals.note: Largest TotalEnergies US renewable PPA. Additive to the ERCOT grid, not behind the meter.
ppaDeals.summary: Google contracted to buy the output of roughly 1 gigawatt of new Texas solar farms for 15 years, which is what allows the developer to raise the money to build them.

ppaDeals.name: Meta and Vistra, three PJM nuclear plants
ppaDeals.type: Nuclear PPA, operating plants plus uprates
ppaDeals.instrument: Executed PPA, operating assets plus committed capacity additions
ppaDeals.structure: 20 year PPAs for more than 2,600MW across three Vistra nuclear plants. Comprises 2,176MW from the operating Perry and Davis Besse plants in Ohio, plus 433MW of incremental capacity from uprates at Perry, Davis Besse, and Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania. Electricity continues to flow to the PJM grid for all users. Largest nuclear uprates supported by a corporate customer in the United States.
ppaDeals.firstPower: Purchases begin late 2026; full 2,609MW online by 2034
ppaDeals.status: Signed. Vistra beginning planning for subsequent licence extensions at all three plants.
ppaDeals.note: The clearest example in the set of a corporate PPA financing new capacity rather than merely contracting existing output. More than 15 percent of contracted capacity is new. Plant capacities: Perry 1,268MW, Davis Besse 908MW, Beaver Valley 1,872MW. Current licences run to 2036, 2037, 2046 and 2047 respectively.

provenance.disclosed: 20 year term, 2,176MW operating plus 433MW uprates, purchases begin late 2026, full volume 2034, named plants and their capacities, current licence expiries, approximately 3,000 project related jobs over roughly nine years
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: total contracted capacity 2,609MW; uprates represent approximately 16.6 percent of contracted capacity
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price per MWh, capacity payment structure

ppaDeals.summary: Meta contracted for 20 years with three nuclear plants in Ohio and Pennsylvania, including funding upgrades that add new capacity rather than just buying existing output.

ppaDeals.name: Clearway portfolio
ppaDeals.type: Grid connected wind and solar PPA
ppaDeals.note: Three projects across Missouri, Texas, West Virginia including Goat Mountain wind repower.
ppaDeals.summary: Google contracted to buy the output of three wind and solar projects across three states for 20 years.

ppaDeals.name: Meta and TerraPower, Natrium units
ppaDeals.instrument: Development funding with rights to future energy. Not an executed PPA on an operating asset.
ppaDeals.structure: Meta funding supports development of two new Natrium units capable of up to 690MW of firm power with delivery as early as 2032, plus rights to energy from up to six further Natrium units capable of 2.1GW targeted for delivery by 2035. Eight potential units in total, 2.8GW of baseload generation capacity plus 1.2GW of built in storage.
ppaDeals.firstPower: As early as 2032 for the first two units; up to 2035 for the remainder
ppaDeals.status: Development stage. TerraPower states its first Natrium plant is under development with design complete, supply chain established, and key regulatory milestones cleared.
ppaDeals.note: Classification matters here. This is funding plus rights to future energy, not contracted offtake from an operating plant. The 2.8GW headline is capacity across eight potential units, of which only two are firmly committed. Meta describes it as its largest support of advanced nuclear technologies to date.

provenance.disclosed: two Natrium units up to 690MW delivery as early as 2032, rights to up to six further units at 2.1GW targeted 2035, eight potential units totalling 2.8GW plus 1.2GW storage
provenance.notDisclosed: funding amount, offtake price, conditions attaching to the rights, what happens if units are not delivered

ppaDeals.summary: Meta is funding the development of new advanced reactors that do not exist yet, with rights to buy the power if they get built, the first as early as 2032.

ppaDeals.name: Meta and Oklo, Pike County Ohio
ppaDeals.instrument: Development funding, pre licence project. Not an executed PPA.
ppaDeals.structure: Meta funding commitment supporting early procurement and development activity for an advanced nuclear campus in Pike County, Ohio, laying the foundation for multiple Oklo Aurora Powerhouse reactors. Up to 1.2GW of baseload power into the PJM market, potentially online as early as 2030.
ppaDeals.status: Development stage. No operating Oklo reactor exists.
ppaDeals.note: Oklo's own chief executive describes the arrangement as a funding commitment in support of early procurement and development activity. Any tracker that adds this 1.2GW to Microsoft's operating 835MW is comparing an aspiration to a contract.

provenance.disclosed: up to 1.2GW, Pike County Ohio, potentially online as early as 2030, PJM delivery, multiple Aurora Powerhouse reactors
provenance.notDisclosed: funding amount, offtake terms, licence status, construction start date

ppaDeals.summary: Meta is funding early development of a nuclear campus in Ohio using reactors that have never been built commercially, potentially online in 2030.

ppaDeals.name: Google and NextEra, Duane Arnold restart
ppaDeals.instrument: Executed PPA, restart of a shut plant
ppaDeals.structure: 25 year agreement for the energy from the restarted 615MW Duane Arnold Energy Center in Palo, Iowa, shut down in 2020. Google purchases power as a 24/7 carbon free source for its cloud and AI infrastructure in Iowa. Central Iowa Power Cooperative purchases the remaining output on the same terms. NextEra has signed definitive agreements to acquire CIPCO and Corn Belt Power Cooperative's combined 30 percent interest, taking its ownership to 100 percent. A separate agreement covers exploring new nuclear generation nationwide.
ppaDeals.firstPower: Targeted fully operational by the first quarter of 2029
ppaDeals.status: Pending NRC and other regulatory approvals to restart.
ppaDeals.note: Note the explicit ratepayer protection language: the PPA enables the investment to restart the plant and covers the costs of production, and Iowa energy customers bear no costs associated with the power Google purchases. That clause is becoming standard in these agreements and is a direct response to the political backlash against data centre load. NextEra now has nearly 3GW of projects executed with Google.

provenance.disclosed: 25 year term, 615MW, Duane Arnold, targeted operational Q1 2029, CIPCO purchasing remaining output on the same terms, NextEra acquiring the 30 percent minority to reach 100 percent ownership, approximately 400 direct full time operations jobs, more than $9B economic benefit to Iowa
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price per MWh, restart capital cost, acquisition price for the 30 percent interest

ppaDeals.summary: Google agreed to buy power for 25 years from an Iowa nuclear plant that shut in 2020, funding its restart, with Iowa customers explicitly bearing none of the cost.

ppaDeals.name: Amazon Web Services and Vistra, Comanche Peak
ppaDeals.parties: Vistra (NYSE: VST) to Amazon Web Services
ppaDeals.structure: 20 year power purchase agreement, with options to extend for up to an additional 20 years, under which Vistra supplies 1,200MW of carbon free power from the Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant in Texas. Power delivery anticipated to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027 and ramp to full capacity by 2032.
ppaDeals.firstPower: Fourth quarter 2027, ramping to full capacity by 2032
ppaDeals.note: Found during source verification and not previously recorded. Note that Vistra's 10-Q describes the counterparty only as a large, investment grade company; the identification as Amazon Web Services comes from Vistra's subsequent earnings call commentary rather than the filing itself. The extension option of up to a further 20 years is unusual and gives the buyer a 40 year potential horizon.

provenance.disclosed: 20 year term with options to extend up to an additional 20 years, 1,200MW, Comanche Peak, delivery beginning Q4 2027 ramping to full capacity by 2032, counterparty described in the filing as a large investment grade company
provenance.analystImputed: counterparty identified as Amazon Web Services based on Vistra earnings call commentary, not stated in the filing
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price per MWh, extension option terms and strike

ppaDeals.summary: Amazon contracted for 1,200 megawatts from a Texas nuclear plant for 20 years, with options to extend for another 20.

ppaDeals.name: Meta and Invenergy, four project portfolio
ppaDeals.structure: Four additional clean energy agreements totalling 791MW of solar and wind. Electricity is delivered to the local grid while Meta receives the clean energy credits associated with the new generation. Brings the companies' total partnership to 1,800MW following 1,000MW announced in 2024.
ppaDeals.note: Named projects: Yellow Wood Solar Ohio 300MW expected 2027, Pleasant Prairie Solar Ohio 140MW expected 2027, Decoy Solar Arkansas 155MW expected 2027, Seaway Wind Texas 196MW expected 2028. Over 740MW of the total is new generation in Ohio, which is where Meta's Prometheus supercluster sits.

provenance.disclosed: 791MW across four named projects with individual capacities and expected commercial operation dates, cumulative 1,800MW partnership, credits structure
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price, term length

ppaDeals.summary: Meta contracted for 791 megawatts of new solar and wind across Ohio, Arkansas and Texas, bringing its total with this developer to 1,800 megawatts.

ppaDeals.name: Amazon and Talen Energy, Susquehanna
ppaDeals.parties: Talen Energy (Nasdaq: TLN) to Amazon Web Services
ppaDeals.type: Nuclear PPA, operating plant, restructured from co located to front of meter
ppaDeals.structure: Expanded PPA under which Talen supplies up to 1,920MW of carbon free nuclear power from Susquehanna through 2042, with options to extend. Delivery ramps over time, expected to reach full volume no later than 2032 with potential to accelerate. Critically, the existing co located load arrangement transitions to a front of the meter arrangement after transmission reconfigurations expected in spring 2026: Susquehanna provides power to the PJM grid, Talen acts as retail electric generation supplier to Amazon, and PPL Electric Utilities is responsible for transmission and delivery.
ppaDeals.firstPower: Ramping, full volume no later than 2032
ppaDeals.status: Signed. Structural transition to front of meter scheduled spring 2026, concurrent with a refuelling outage.
ppaDeals.powerRoute: Front of meter, restructured from behind the meter
ppaDeals.note: The most instructive power deal in the database. The original behind the meter co located arrangement was restructured into a front of the meter supply arrangement, which is what happens when a regulator declines to bless a structure that bypasses the grid and its cost allocation. Talen frames the benefit in credit terms: a long term steady source of revenue, greater balance sheet flexibility through contracted revenues, significantly decreased market risk, and reduced reliance on the federal nuclear production tax credit. Amazon separately cites a $20 billion Pennsylvania investment.

provenance.disclosed: 1,920MW at full contract quantity, through 2042 with extension options, full volume no later than 2032, transition to front of meter after spring 2026 transmission reconfigurations, PPL as transmission provider, Talen as retail supplier, Amazon $20B Pennsylvania investment, more than 900 employees at the facility
provenance.notDisclosed: contract price, ramp schedule by year, extension terms, the economics of the front of meter transition

ppaDeals.summary: Amazon contracted for 1,920 megawatts from a Pennsylvania nuclear plant through 2042, and the arrangement was restructured so the power goes through the public grid rather than directly to the data centre.

ppaDeals.name: Meta and Constellation, Clinton Clean Energy Center
ppaDeals.structure: 20 year PPA for the output of the Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois, beginning June 2027, supporting relicensing and continued operation for another two decades after the state ratepayer funded zero emission credit programme expires. Meta purchases the plant's clean energy attributes.
ppaDeals.market: MISO zone four, central and southern Illinois
ppaDeals.note: A market based replacement for a state subsidy. Constellation describes the deal as essentially replacing the ZEC programme and securing long term operation without ratepayer support. Also adds 30MW through uprates and preserves roughly 1,100 jobs with $13.5mm of annual tax revenue.

provenance.disclosed: 20 year term, 1,121MW, start June 2027, 30MW uprate, 1,100 jobs preserved, $13.5mm annual taxes, $1mm charitable giving over five years, ZEC programme expiry context
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price, whether Meta takes physical power or attributes only in full

ppaDeals.summary: Meta agreed to buy the output of an Illinois nuclear plant for 20 years, replacing a state subsidy that was about to expire and keeping the plant open.

ppaDeals.name: Google and Elementl Power
ppaDeals.instrument: Early stage development capital with an option for offtake. Not a PPA.
ppaDeals.structure: Strategic agreement to pre position three project sites for advanced nuclear energy. Google commits early stage development capital to advance the three projects. Each project would generate at least 600MW, with the option for commercial offtake once complete. Technology agnostic; Elementl continues evaluating reactor technology, EPC and other project partners.
ppaDeals.status: Site pre positioning stage. No technology selected, no EPC contract, no licence.
ppaDeals.note: The clearest case in the database of a headline gigawatt figure that is not contracted capacity. Google commits development capital and holds an option to buy power if the projects are ever completed. Elementl's own goal is more than 10GW online by 2035. Elementl was founded in 2022 and is backed by Breakwater North and Energy Impact Partners.

provenance.disclosed: three sites, each at least 600MW, early stage development capital from Google, option for commercial offtake once complete, technology agnostic approach, Elementl 10GW ambition by 2035
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: implied minimum aggregate capacity 1,800MW across the three sites
provenance.notDisclosed: capital committed, option strike or pricing, site locations, technology, timeline

sources.label: Elementl Power release via PR Newswire, 7 May 2025

ppaDeals.summary: Google is funding the early groundwork on three potential nuclear sites and holds an option to buy the power if they are ever completed, with no technology chosen yet.

ppaDeals.name: Amazon and X-energy
ppaDeals.parties: Amazon Climate Pledge Fund, Ken Griffin, Ares Management affiliates, NGP, University of Michigan into X-energy
ppaDeals.type: Equity investment plus SMR development collaboration
ppaDeals.instrument: Series C-1 equity financing plus a deployment target. Not a contracted PPA.
ppaDeals.structure: Approximately $500 million Series C-1 financing round anchored by Amazon, funding completion of X-energy's reactor design and licensing and the first phase of its TRISO-X fuel fabrication facility. Separately, Amazon and X-energy target more than 5GW of new power projects across the United States by 2039 through direct project investments and long term PPAs. Initial four unit 320MW project with Energy Northwest in central Washington, with an option to increase to 12 units and 960MW.
ppaDeals.status: Investment closed. Initial project in early development.
ppaDeals.note: IMPORTANT CORRECTION. The round is approximately $500 million, not the $700 million widely reported, and Amazon anchored it rather than providing all of it. The more than 5GW figure is a joint deployment target by 2039, not contracted capacity. Only the 320MW Energy Northwest project has a named counterparty and site. Each Xe-100 unit is 80MW, with plants configured from 320MW to 960MW. Moelis acted as exclusive financial adviser and placement agent to X-energy.

provenance.disclosed: approximately $500mm Series C-1 anchored by Amazon, named co investors, more than 5GW target by 2039, initial 320MW four unit project with Energy Northwest, option to 12 units and 960MW, 80MW per unit, Moelis as adviser
provenance.notDisclosed: Amazon's share of the round, PPA prices, project level investment amounts, timeline beyond the initial project

ppaDeals.summary: Amazon led a $500 million investment into a small reactor developer and set a joint target of building more than 5 gigawatts by 2039, starting with a 320 megawatt project in Washington state.

ppaDeals.name: Google and Kairos Power
ppaDeals.type: Advanced nuclear master development agreement with PPAs
ppaDeals.instrument: Master Plant Development Agreement with PPAs attaching to plants not yet built
ppaDeals.structure: Master Plant Development Agreement creating a path to deploy a United States fleet of advanced nuclear projects totalling 500MW by 2035. Kairos will develop, construct and operate a series of advanced reactor plants and sell energy, ancillary services, and environmental attributes to Google under power purchase agreements. Plants sited in relevant service territories to supply Google data centres, with first deployment by 2030. Milestone based accountability is built into the agreement.
ppaDeals.firstPower: First deployment by 2030; fleet total by 2035
ppaDeals.status: Development. The NRC issued a construction permit for Kairos's Hermes demonstration reactor in 2023, the first non water cooled reactor approved for construction in the US in more than 50 years.
ppaDeals.note: Described as the first corporate agreement for multiple deployments of a single advanced reactor design in the United States. The PPAs are real but they attach to plants that do not yet exist, which is a different credit proposition from an operating asset. Google has signed more than 115 clean energy agreements totalling over 14GW since 2010.

provenance.disclosed: 500MW by 2035, first deployment by 2030, Master Plant Development Agreement structure, PPAs covering energy, ancillary services and environmental attributes, milestone based accountability, Hermes construction permit 2023
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price, milestone definitions, consequences of missed milestones

ppaDeals.summary: Google agreed to buy power from a fleet of advanced reactors totalling 500 megawatts, the first expected by 2030, from a company whose demonstration reactor is still under construction.

ppaDeals.name: Microsoft and Constellation, Crane Clean Energy Center
ppaDeals.instrument: Executed PPA, restart of a shut plant
ppaDeals.structure: 20 year power purchase agreement enabling the restart of Three Mile Island Unit 1, relaunched as the Crane Clean Energy Center. Microsoft purchases energy from the renewed plant to match its PJM data centre consumption with carbon free energy. Constellation's largest ever PPA.
ppaDeals.status: Restart requires NRC approval plus state and local permits. Constellation separately pursuing licence renewal to extend operations to at least 2054.
ppaDeals.note: IMPORTANT CORRECTION. The widely repeated $16 billion contract value does not appear in Constellation's press release. The release discloses no contract value at all. Any $16B figure is an analyst estimate, not a disclosed term. Note also the release states expected online 2028, not 2027 as several trackers report.

provenance.disclosed: 20 year term, 835MW, TMI Unit 1 restart, Crane Clean Energy Center naming, online expected 2028, licence renewal target 2054, 3,400 direct and indirect jobs, more than $3B in state and federal taxes, largest PPA in Constellation's history
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price per MWh, ramp schedule, termination provisions

ppaDeals.summary: Microsoft agreed to buy the power from a shut down nuclear reactor at Three Mile Island for 20 years, which is what pays for restarting it.

ppaDeals.name: Microsoft and Brookfield renewable framework
ppaDeals.parties: Brookfield Asset Management and Brookfield Renewable to Microsoft
ppaDeals.instrument: Framework agreement, a pathway to deliver rather than contracted capacity
ppaDeals.structure: Five year global framework agreement providing a pathway for Brookfield to deliver over 10.5GW of new renewable energy capacity between 2026 and 2030 in the United States and Europe, with potential to expand scope to Asia Pacific, India, and Latin America. Supports Microsoft's goal of matching 100 percent of electricity consumption with zero carbon purchases by 2030.
ppaDeals.status: Framework signed. Almost 1GW contracted separately outside the agreement prior to signing.
ppaDeals.note: Described as almost eight times larger than the largest single corporate PPA ever signed at the time. But it is a framework providing a pathway, not a single executed PPA, and individual projects are contracted underneath it. The instrument distinction is the same one that applies across the nuclear set.

provenance.disclosed: over 10.5GW, five year agreement, delivery window 2026 to 2030, US and Europe with potential expansion, almost 1GW already contracted outside the agreement, described as almost eight times the largest single corporate PPA
provenance.notDisclosed: contract value, price, project level detail, binding commitment level

ppaDeals.summary: A five year framework under which Brookfield may deliver over 10.5 gigawatts of renewable power to Microsoft, with individual projects contracted underneath it.

maDeals.name: Aligned Data Centers acquisition
maDeals.acquirer: Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Partnership (AIP), MGX, and BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP)
maDeals.seller: Private infrastructure funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management and co invest partners
maDeals.structure: Consortium acquisition of 100 percent of the equity in Aligned Data Centers. Enterprise value of approximately $40 billion. An additional $5 billion of growth capital committed at closing to fund continued expansion. Existing management continues to lead the company, which remains headquartered in Dallas.
maDeals.buyerType: Consortium: sovereign wealth, infrastructure funds, and an AI infrastructure vehicle
maDeals.rationale: AIP's first investment, and a step toward its initial target of mobilising and deploying $30 billion of equity capital with the potential to support up to $100 billion of total investment including debt. Aligned holds 51 campuses and more than 6.4GW of operational and planned capacity across Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, Ohio, Phoenix, Salt Lake City, Sao Paulo, Queretaro and Santiago.
maDeals.note: The largest transaction in the database and one of the largest private investments ever made in digital infrastructure. Note the buyer composition: MGX is an Abu Dhabi technology investment company and GIP is part of BlackRock with over $200 billion under management. This is sovereign and institutional capital taking out a private infrastructure fund at scale, which is the exit path the sector's earlier investors were underwriting.

provenance.disclosed: completed 21 July 2026, approximately $40B enterprise value, 100 percent of equity acquired, seller Macquarie Asset Management funds and co invest partners, additional $5B growth capital committed at closing, 51 campuses and more than 6.4GW operational and planned, AIP targets $30B equity and up to $100B total, GIP over $200B AUM, management retained
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: implied enterprise value per GW of operational and planned capacity is approximately $6.25B
provenance.notDisclosed: debt quantum and terms, equity split between consortium members, Macquarie's entry cost and return, breakdown of operational versus planned capacity

sources.label: Aligned Data Centers press release, 21 July 2026

financingDeals.name: Nvidia AI factory financing platforms
financingDeals.summary: Nvidia and six of the world's largest infrastructure investors are creating repeatable financing platforms designed to mobilise over $500 billion of third party capital for AI data centres, with Nvidia offering limited residual value support on some projects.
financingDeals.parties: Nvidia with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR
financingDeals.structure: Independent financing platforms intended to mobilise more than $500 billion of third party capital over time to fund AI factory buildout. Nvidia provides the compute platform; the financial institutions provide long term capital and independently underwrite each opportunity on customer, demand, utilisation, cash flow and residual value. Nvidia states the $500 billion figure is aggregate third party capital the platforms are designed to mobilise over time, and is not Nvidia revenue, a single fund, or a commitment to a single customer. The platforms are aimed at qualified AI labs, enterprises and AI clouds that have compute demand but lack access to financing at the required scale or cost.
financingDeals.creditSupport: Nvidia may provide a residual value support mechanism for up to 25 percent of an opportunity, assessed project by project. Nvidia describes this as substantially lower than other compute financing arrangements, and justifies its willingness on the grounds that its compute is fungible, universally adopted, software upgradable and redeployable.
financingDeals.note: The thesis becoming an asset class. Nvidia's explicit argument is that compute should be financed as productive infrastructure rather than project by project, and its case for residual value rests on three claims: fungibility across customers and workloads, software upgrades that improve installed hardware over its life, and demonstrated longevity, citing the 2020 A100 still in active commercial use six years later with an economic life extending toward a decade. Note the deliberate contrast on support levels: Nvidia caps itself at 25 percent of an opportunity while Broadcom's residual value support on the Compute SPV covered roughly $30 billion of a $35 billion financing, close to 86 percent. Nvidia also addresses the circularity question directly, arguing that independent underwriting by third party capital is the answer.

pricingData.h100OneYearRental: approximately $1.70 per GPU hour in October 2025 rising to approximately $2.35 in March 2026
pricingData.crossProviderOnDemandMedian: approximately $2.00 per GPU hour in October 2025 rising to $2.70 in June 2026

sources.label: Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO, post on X, August 2026

provenance.disclosed: six named partners, more than $500B of third party capital designed to be mobilised over time, residual value support up to 25 percent of an opportunity assessed project by project, H100 one year rental $1.70 October 2025 to $2.35 March 2026, cross provider on demand median $2.00 October 2025 to $2.70 June 2026, B200 cloud rates approximately $5.30 to $7.05, A100 introduced 2020 still in active commercial use, characterisation of the $500B figure as aggregate and not revenue
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: on demand median GPU hour pricing rose approximately 35 percent between October 2025 and June 2026; H100 one year rental rose approximately 38 percent over five months; Nvidia's stated 25 percent support cap compares with roughly 86 percent residual value support on the Broadcom backed Compute SPV
provenance.notDisclosed: platform structures, individual fund sizes, fees, terms of the residual value support, which partners cover which segments, deployment timeline, what qualifies a customer

financingDeals.sourceNote: Primary statement by the company chief executive, published on X rather than as a corporate release. Replace with the Nvidia newsroom URL if an equivalent post exists there.

financingDeals.name: Google TPU supply programme for Anthropic (umbrella)
financingDeals.parties: Google / Broadcom / Anthropic / Apollo / Blackstone / Morgan Stanley / crypto miner developers
financingDeals.structure: Three way division of balance sheet risk. Google guarantees the data centre leases. Broadcom buys the chips from Google and helps finance them. Apollo and Blackstone anchor private credit that purchases the hardware and leases it to Anthropic. Morgan Stanley arranged the vehicle, described in reporting as an adaptation of the Boeing and GE vendor financing model for aircraft and engines. Stated motive: no participant wanted tens of billions of AI chips on its balance sheet. Google is already at record capex; Broadcom is the financing provider but does not want to be in the financing business.
financingDeals.creditSupport: Google guarantees on 10 developments totalling 2.4GW of power for TPUs. Maximum exposure if all leases go bad is as much as $44B; the liability is marked at $815MM on Google's balance sheet. Google may also step into the leases itself.
financingDeals.note: This is the umbrella programme; the Nexus Hubbard, TeraWulf and Hut8 records are components of it. Key structural reading: the chips are financed separately from the buildings, by different parties, on different instruments. Private credit owns the hardware and leases it; Google guarantees the real estate. Direct quote from a Google executive involved: each participant is putting its balance sheet to work, Google on the data centre side and Broadcom on the chip side. KEY VALIDATION: $35M per MW for silicon against roughly $10M per MW for standard air cooled shell construction gives a silicon to steel ratio of about 3.5 to 1, confirming the deck sandwich estimate of $25M to $40M per MW of IT hardware derived in module 1 of the curriculum.

detail.googleStakeInTenant: 14% of Anthropic per legal filings, capped at 15%, non voting, no board seats and no board observer rights

financingDeals.structure: Closing of a $1.025 billion zero coupon convertible senior notes offering. Convertible notes are debt that may convert into equity at a set price, and a zero coupon structure means no cash interest is paid, with the lender compensated by the conversion option instead.
financingDeals.creditSupport: None. This is corporate level convertible debt raised on TeraWulf's own balance sheet, not project financing supported by a third party guarantee.

When Google guarantees its lease, the same company accesses a $3.2B construction bond. Two financings by the same borrower, one with credit support and one without, which is the clearest single illustration of what a guarantee is worth.

structuralPatterns: Vendor residual value support is being standardised and priced. Broadcom's support on the Compute SPV covered roughly 86 percent of a $35 billion financing. Nvidia has since announced platforms capping its own residual value support at 25 percent of an opportunity, explicitly describing that as substantially lower than other compute financing arrangements. The instrument is the same; the coverage level is now a competitive variable.

Credit support is compensated with equity or equity linked instruments rather than cash fees: Meta at 20 percent of Hyperion, Equinix xScale at 80/20, Google penny warrants in TeraWulf, Google at roughly 20 percent of the Nexus Hubbard project.
Guarantees are written options, not accommodations. Google marks a $44B maximum exposure at $815MM carrying value, implying an expected payout probability under 2 percent.

The cost of capital spread is the price of the wrapper: Google backed data centre projects borrowed at a median 7.1 percent against 9.3 percent for neocloud operators around Nvidia chips, roughly 220 basis points.
Chips and buildings are financed separately, by different parties, on different instruments. Private credit owns the silicon and leases it; investment grade balance sheets guarantee the real estate.
Silicon runs roughly 3.5x steel per megawatt: approximately $35M per MW for TPU hardware against approximately $10M per MW for standard air cooled shell construction.
Behind the meter generation is displacing utility interconnection as the power route, moving the binding constraint from transmission to gas pipeline capacity.
Sovereign capital has entered the stack, with recoupment then residual split structures that mirror preferred return and promote waterfalls.

Headline nuclear capacity is mostly not contracted capacity. Across the announced hyperscaler nuclear deals, roughly 5.1GW sits under executed PPAs on operating or restarting plants, while the remainder of the widely cited 9.8GW consists of development funding, options, and in one case a memorandum of understanding. Instrument classification changes the number by nearly half.

Regulators are pushing co located load back onto the grid. The Amazon and Talen arrangement at Susquehanna converted from a behind the meter co located structure to a front of the meter supply arrangement with the utility responsible for transmission, which is the clearest signal available that bypassing grid cost allocation is not a settled strategy.
openQuestions: Does the 220 basis point wrapper spread compress as the structure becomes standard?
Do Compute SPV style tranches ever trade or get rated, creating a public price for TPU and GPU residual risk?
Does gas pipeline capacity become the next queue, or does behind the meter simply relocate the constraint?
How much of announced capacity converts to energized capacity, against a historical 24 to 40 percent range?
Does the ratepayer protection language now appearing in these agreements, stating that local customers bear no cost for the power the buyer purchases, become a standard condition of approval?
